title: Violent death and bog deposition of Lindow Man
summary: Lindow Man is a preserved bog body recovered from Lindow Moss. Physical investigation supports a violent death followed by deposition in the bog. The exact date and motive remain debated; this EVENT record intentionally does not encode ritual sacrifice as historical fact.

time.note: Broad radiocarbon range reported in British Museum review; spans late Iron Age into Roman-period Britain.

historicity.note: Confidence covers violent death and bog deposition, not motive.

uncertainty: The precise dating remains a range.
The sequence and interpretation of injuries has been debated.
Ritual sacrifice is a hypothesis, not an EVENT fact.
alternative_interpretations: Execution, homicide, or another violent-death context not demonstrably ritual.

review.note: Canonical only for material event context: violent death and bog deposition.
